summary: Shanghai is best for stylish urban travel shaped by waterfront icons, historic-modern contrast, elegant streets, and polished evening atmosphere.
transport_notes: Shanghai works best when each day is organized by district rather than trying to cross the city repeatedly.
Metro is strong, but plans should still avoid stacking far-apart riverside, old-city, and former concession areas on the same day.
Couple-oriented evenings are strongest when the route ends near the Bund, riverfront, or a slower-designed street district.

budget_notes.low: Focus on street wandering, riverfront views, and approachable neighborhood food rather than premium dining.
budget_notes.medium: Blend one signature skyline or heritage zone with one design-forward street area and one reliable dining cluster each day.
budget_notes.high: Add stronger atmosphere-led dining, slower boutique pacing, and polished evening districts.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans should make Shanghai feel energetic, photogenic, and still financially manageable.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize observing city texture, architecture, and neighborhood contrast at a personal pace.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should highlight skyline romance, stylish streets, evening reflections, and strong photo moments.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should simplify movement and balance landmark moments with gentler public spaces.
